transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… I just feel like I’m constantly running on a motor lately. I finish something at school or at home and then I’m immediately onto the next thing. It’s like I can’t really shut myself off.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
I’m not really sure. I mean… sometimes I probably do, but I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Can you think of a recent time when you did something without thinking it through?

Yeah… I guess recently I’ve been cutting into conversations. Like at work, with colleagues or parents, or even at home with my wife and relatives. I think I’m helping or moving things along, but I end up talking over people before they’re finished.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Yeah… pretty often. In meetings, like IEP meetings or my admin classes, I’ll catch my leg bouncing under the table, or I’m clicking a pen, shifting around in the chair. Sometimes I don’t even notice until someone glances over.
Do you often talk more than others in social situations?

Yeah… I think I do. In parent conferences or staff meetings, I’ll plan to keep it short, and then I’m giving multiple examples, telling some classroom story, adding ideas nobody asked for. Sometimes I can tell the other person is trying to wrap it up, and I’m still talking.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?
I’m not sure… I mean, I haven’t really paid much attention to that specifically. I can get pulled off sometimes, I guess, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal.
As a child, were you often described as restless or having a lot of energy?

Yeah… from what I’ve been told, yes. My mother used to joke that I was kind of “teaching the class from my seat” in elementary school—out of my chair, talking, cutting in before the teacher finished. So… it wasn’t really new as an adult.
Did you have difficulty engaging in quiet leisure activities as a child?

I don’t remember the child part very clearly. But even now, quiet time is… hard. If my spouse is watching a show or someone’s resting, I’ll start humming or talking through what I’m doing, moving stuff around, and eventually someone asks me to settle down.
Do you often have mood swings?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t really call them mood swings. I can get irritated sometimes, but I haven’t really tracked it or thought of it that way.
Do you often have difficulty sustaining focus during tasks or activities?
I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I haven’t really paid attention to it in that way. Some tasks, maybe, but… I don’t know.
As a child, did you have trouble sitting still or being quiet for a long time?

Yeah… I think so. My mother used to say I was “teaching the class from my seat” in elementary school. I was out of my chair a lot, talking, cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So… it was there pretty early, I guess.
Have you often interrupted your spouse or others during conversations at home?

Yeah… I do. More than I’d like to admit. At home I’ll jump in when my wife’s talking with someone, or even with relatives, and I think I’m helping clarify things. But I end up talking over them or kind of taking over before they’re finished.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're not in a meeting or a classroom?

Yeah… I guess I do. Even in IEP meetings or my admin classes, my leg’s usually bouncing under the table, or I’m clicking a pen. Sometimes I’m shifting around enough that people look over before I even notice I’m doing it.
Have you experienced these symptoms of restlessness and difficulty focusing your entire life?

Yeah… I mean, as far back as I can remember, it was kind of there. My mom used to joke that in elementary school I was “teaching the class from my seat” because I’d be out of my chair, talking, cutting in before the teacher finished. So it wasn’t something that just started recently or with the family stuff.
Have these symptoms caused problems for you at work or in your relationships?

Yeah… it has. Work especially. The complaints got serious enough that I was put on a corrective plan, which is… hard to say.

And at home, my wife says the caregiving routines are harder because people are managing my energy too, on top of everything else. I don’t mean to make things harder, but I think I’ve damaged some trust with colleagues and family, even when I’m trying to help.
Were you physically very active as a child, such as running, climbing, or having trouble staying still during play?

Yeah… I think so. My mom used to say I was basically “teaching the class from my seat” in elementary school. I was always up, talking, cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So… it was there pretty early, not just something that showed up later.
Have you ever lost a job or had significant problems in your relationships because of your difficulty with restlessness, impulsivity, or inattention?

I haven’t lost a job, no. But it’s been… close enough to scare me. The complaints at work got serious, and I was put on a corrective plan.

At home, my wife says the caregiving routines are harder because everyone’s kind of managing my energy too. I don’t like admitting that. I think I’ve hurt some trust with people at work and with family, even when I’m trying to help.
Have you had any long-term friendships or relationships that have lasted without significant strain or difficulty due to your behavior?

I mean… some relationships have lasted, yes. But I wouldn’t say without strain.

At work, it’s gotten serious enough that I was put on a corrective plan. And at home, my wife has said the caregiving routines are harder because people are kind of managing my energy too. I don’t like saying that, but… I do feel like I’ve damaged trust with colleagues and family, even when I’m trying to help.
Have you ever felt like your symptoms have significantly impacted your ability to function effectively in your daily life or relationships?

Yes. I mean… I don’t like putting it that strongly, but yes.

At work, the complaints got serious enough that I was put on a corrective plan. And at home, my wife says routines—especially caregiving stuff—are harder because people are also having to manage my energy. I think I’ve damaged some trust with coworkers and family, even when I’m trying to help.
Do you often have trouble following through on instructions or finishing tasks at work or at home?
I’m not sure. I mean, I get things done… maybe not always smoothly, but I’d have to think about specific examples. I don’t know that I’d say “often” without knowing what you mean exactly.
